title: Capacity-on-demand broker and staggered overage accounting for temporary uplifts
creator: Ava Park
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated occasionally need short-lived extra throughput (e.g., launch day traffic, nightly batch jobs). Current behavior grants transient capacity but invoices customers with a single overage line item that is hard to attribute and often causes disputes. We need a broker that mediates short-term capacity uplifts ("on-demand uplifts") and a staggered overage accounting model that smooths invoice exposure and provides clear attribution.
acceptance_criteria: Broker accepts uplift requests and returns an allocation token within 200ms for requests within policy limits
Allocated uplift tokens reserve capacity and are visible in Console (tenant + token ID) within 30s
Billing records show per-token metering windows and apply graduated pricing tiers for 0-15m, 15-60m, >60m
Reconciler job matches uplift tokens to actual usage and produces an invoice draft with line-level attribution
Operator can force-revoke or extend single tokens via operator API and Console
Rollout to 10% of tenants on dedicated fleets with no SLO regressions (p95 latency < 200ms for normal inference requests)
tasks: Design broker API and token lifecycle (request, allocate, heartbeat, revoke)
Implement broker service with connection to fleet allocator and quota manager
Add token-level metering hooks to existing metering pipeline
Implement staggered billing rules in billing reconciler (configurable bands)
Console: token list view, operator controls, and per-token cost preview
E2E tests: allocation race conditions, operator overrides, billing reconciliation
Create runbook for operators (revoke, extend, dispute handling)
Prepare customer-facing FAQ and billing example scenarios
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use a short-lived allocation token (UUID) instead of modifying route-level config — tokens are easier to attribute and revoke
Trade-off: Keeping allocation tokens distinct increases bookkeeping but prevents accidental global autoscale changes
We will implement graduated billing bands rather than per-minute flat rate to reduce invoice shock for very short spikes
Broker will refuse allocations that would violate fleet-level throughput guarantees; fallback: enqueue request or return soft-failure code with recommended wait
Operator override will mark tokens as 'admin-extended' to prevent automatic expiry for troubleshooting
telemetry_and_metrics: Allocation request rate (req/s) and success ratio
Token utilization: reserved v. consumed token-seconds
Burst-related latency delta for tenants using uplift tokens (p50/p95)
Billing reconciliation mismatch rate (tokens without matching usage records)
Number of operator revocations and reason codes
rollout_plan: Canary: onboard internal beta tenants and enable broker by default for test fleets
Phase 1 (10% tenants): token issuance + read-only Console views + billing drafts (no live invoices)
Phase 2 (50% tenants): enable operator controls and live invoices with clear line attribution
Phase 3 (100% tenants): enable automatic self-serve uplift in Console and public docs
Fallbacks: if reconciler mismatch > 0.5% during Phase 1, pause issuance and run reconciler in audit-only mode
testing_plan: Unit tests for broker token lifecycle and expiry edge cases
Chaos test: simulate sudden fleet preemption and ensure tokens are revoked and customers receive notifications
Billing integration tests with sandbox ledger and sample tenant data
Load test: allocation service at 10k req/s sustained to validate latency targets
Manual operator drills to revoke/extend tokens and confirm Console state changes
